Every bad ending feels cheap, and the general writing is cringe. There is no creepy horror atmosphere despite this being a horror visual novel. The True End was also boring and made everything MC went through feel pointless.

[i]BAD END[/i] (2015) delivers a mildly unsettling yet addictive horror-themed mystery experience, with 100% of Steam achievements unlocked in just 2.2 hours. Ideal for fans of short investigative visual novels with eerie tension, the game centers around uncovering the truth behind a best friend’s sudden, mysterious, and untimely demise at the hands of a strange game rumored to kill its players if they make the wrong choices and reach bad endings.

The main objective is to uncover the supernatural truth and deduce the nature and identity of a shadowy, mysterious entity through both in-game and real-world investigations. Bad endings can be triggered during key points of the investigation by making any two incorrect choices while playing the cursed game, while other non-canonical endings occur through mistakes made in real-world interactions, such as getting cold feet and abandoning the playthrough. 

The eerie, haunting atmosphere is well-supported by the music, which consistently builds tension and maintains a sense of unease. Tracks such as Fear, Despair, and Wirepuller help heighten the intensity, creating a sense of nervousness and restlessness. Despite its darker premise, the true ending resolves key plotlines and offers a satisfying, happy, and ultimately positive conclusion for the protagonist, making the journey feel worthwhile. [i]BAD END[/i] (2015) is, therefore, best approached as a short but memorable mystery-horror story that delivers tension and intrigue.

BAD END is a B-movie-esque, contrived visual novel, but it's surprisingly not [i]too[/i] bad.

The synopsis is basically what it says on the box: Kyuuhei's friend Yuuji dies while playing the mystery-surrounded, supposedly death-inducing mobile game BAD END, and then, at least in the true route, Kyuuhei plays the game himself to discover how it caused Yuuji's death.

The writing quality and premise are, again, at the level of a B-movie, but I can sometimes be pretty partial to those types of stories. I'd almost say I liked BAD END, but it was the number of endings and process of reaching them that soured it for me to the level of ambivalence. It turns out that BAD END (the game within the game) gives [spoiler]you one freebie—you don't immediately die if you reach one bad end, but you do die if you reach two.[/spoiler] Half of the endings in the game stop there, and play in the more or less the same way every time. And the other endings beside the true ending aren't much better. It's not surprising that a game called BAD END has a lot of bad endings, but that doesn't mean that I like them.

Overall, BAD END is mediocre. It seems like it goes on sale often and for very cheap, and it's only about two hours long, so if nothing else, it could be a decent time killer, but don't go into expecting to be blown away.

VN sympatoche qui se boucle en 3h grand max qui se divise en 2 histoires parallèles :
- La 1ère est celle du protagoniste qui après la mort d'un de ses potes des suites d'un jeu dans lequel perdre signifie la mort dans la réalité, décide de s'y mettre aussi tout en enquêtant pour découvrir l'origine de ce jeu.
- la 2ème est celle du jeu maudit lui même baptisé "BAD END" qui suit une étudiante poursuivie par une entité malfaisante et hostile dont le seul but est de la tuée.

Chaque affrontement vous donne plusieurs choix à faire, et faire le mauvais signifie la mort aussi bien pour le personnage que pour le joueur et donne donc accès à l'une des nombreuses fins et à un succès (ce qui poussera les complétistes à mourir un bon nombre de fois :) ) mais le jeu grand seigneur vous accorde tout de même un droit à l'erreur sans répercutions funeste.

Le scénario est assez classique et efficace mais ne surprendra personne qui a déjà eu à faire avec des histoire à base d'objet maudit dans la lignée de Ring et consort. 
Mais le jeu est suffisamment court pour pouvoir être bouclé en une session de jeu (ce fût mon cas) et peux vous comblez si vous n'avez rien à vous mettre sous la dent ou aucune envie de vous lancez dans un gros jeu qui va vous accaparer de nombreuse heures. 

Un dernier mot au sujet de la traduction française...
Je la qualifiais de fonctionnelle. Pas d'énorme fotes d'ortogrfe mais beaucoup de problème de conjugaisons. Énormément de phrases sont eu présent de l'indicatif alors qu'elle ne devrait pas l’être
Exemple: un perso se souvient soudainement de quelque chose et dit "J'entend ça quelque part" au lieu de "J'ai entendu ça quelque part" 
Vers la fin du jeu plusieurs phrases au sens improbable te saute  à la gueule, bref c'est une VF torchée vite fait mais qui vous n'emperchera pas de comprendre l'histoire. Et pour avoir fait un rapide p"tit tour, la version anglaise n'a pas l'air particulièrement mieux lottie.

Well, I have to admit to be pleasantly surprised. I think this is a solid story. It's exactly how the characters "out of the game" describe it, in that it doesn't look like too much at first, but it has layers upon layers. And the ending was satifying, something I have to be honest, I didn't expect from the subject matter. I have to give my kudos to the writer. Even if the text wanders here and there (see my notes about translation), the story is conveyed and it's good.

Which in this case it's a bit of a shame. Honestly, I have grips with the fact the subject theme was wasted on the UI and general presentation. The story is literally about a game (within a game). So, why the visuals didn't reflect this? 

For example, when inside the girl's game, it would have been nice to see the difference with the "real life" look. Maybe add a frame, like that of a cellphone, and a vertical presentation only for that part of the story. A GUI inside the GUI. Or a filter that makes everything look like you're looking at the screen. There's so many missed opportunities. 

Besides, it's ridiculous that the "in game" sprites look exactly like the "out game" ones. There should have been a shift there - hell, that could have been scary to see something there resemble the other reality, while not quite fitting in it.

There's also the issue the sprites almost don't move. At first I found myself looking at the screen, trying to figure out who was talking. You don't have to animate the mouth, but at least make the mouth open (or the sprites jump?) to indicate who's talking. 

The lack of sound design also. Reading "gah irk ugh" and all those other suggested dying sounds... you know how effective it would have been if I could have heard the voice? 

Just mentioning these things because I feel the writing deserve better. That said, and despite all my praise of the writing, there are some obvious issues, of course. For one, the translation is bad... it takes me out from the immersion of the story when everything sounds unnatural/fake or it's near impossible to understand (I played it in English, for clarification. I could try the Spanish version to see if it's a problem that carries there too. But I'm guessing it doesn't sound like this in the original language.). 

Other than that, the choices placement is good, and the story gets you interested... even if the fact is you don't get a clue what is a good and bad choice... especially in the begining. You are bound do die, and that takes away from the initial tension of making a mistake by the next time you make a choice. This may be by design, though... the writers might have thought it was too much tension XD

So all in all, a solid 7/10 in writing, 6/10 everything else. 


Btw, I haven't been able to get Bad End 5. If somebody has any guide on how to get that, please and thank you.

BAD END is a short horror visual novel with a bit of a clique plot and some unintentional funny moments. 

The overall game is fairly short, about an hour or two depending on how fast you read, but it makes up for the length with the amount of possible endings it has. Getting the bad endings is fairly easy and doesn't really require a guide to figure them out, as from playing it blind you're more than likely to come across at least one during a playthrough. The choices will have a 1/3 or 1/2 chance on being the correct one so choosing the wrong ones isn't so difficult. The catch though is you have to get it wrong twice in a row in some places to get that bad end.

As for the plot, yeah, it's a little generic and the horror isn't really that scary but I did like the characters for the most part.

For what it's worth, it's really not a bad game despite its flaws, plus it's pretty cheap so you can't really go wrong there. Overall though, I would recommend it for those who enjoy the horror vn genre.

Bad End is a story about a mobile game that kills the player if he or she dies in the game.

Decent artwork and good plot development are the main strong points of the novel.

This is a story-driven game. The plot itself screams horror, but unfortunately the game does not delve much into it; i.e. no scare jump scenes, relatively little gore, etc. Which is a pity. For example, the main character can die at many times during the story, yet the story barely delves into each; i.e. no artwork, just a plain text explanation of the death.

Game uses generic music obtained from online sources. While mostly ok, it is not unique to the game, and at time fails to fit the mood of the story, especially on the more sombre parts.

Summary: I do recommend the game, but would wait for a sale. 6/10.

Original review:
I honestly hesitate to "not recommend" BAD END, as I do so based purely on the content and not on the gameplay. The gameplay is fine. The translation is... fine. Not the worst I've ever read, but not perfect. The character art is passable, though the lack of changing character models, or even assigned colored text boxes for the characters makes it incredibly difficult to track who is speaking at times. The background art is actually quite well done. Finally, I'll note that while steam lists this game as having full controller support, and the in-game menu gives a single controller option, my controllers (xbox 360 wired and new xbox wireless) didn't work. 

BAD END is just a boring, lazily written story, with boring characters who have one-dimensional motivations. I am particularly resistant to horror as a genre, so I don't typically rate "horror" content based on how scary I find it- but BAD END isn't even reminiscent of horror for me because the overarching mystery isn't compelling enough to carry the story. I respect that the developers didn't resort to filling their game with jump scares (well, except one, but that one isn't really in the game), but this VN reads like a teen drama with supernatural elements. A bad teen drama.

If you want a good mystery (not quite scary but still horror-like) VN, PLEASE skip this and read 'The Letter', or 'Raging Loop' instead. Both are available on steam and are much longer (I have over 100+ hours in The Letter, and Raging Loop takes about 40 to complete) with great stories. The Letter has jump scares, Raging Loop doesn't.

Our main character Kyuuhei's goal is to get to the truth of their childhood friend's death. To do so, he literally risks his life, knowingly, just to find closure about this horrific event. There are 14 endings in this game and at the very end of the true ending, Kyuuhei says this:

[spoiler] "I lost my best friend to this whole tragedy, but in the end I at least got sum bussy*."  [/spoiler] 

This right here can be considered as a character error because of the two opposite thoughts going on in this ♥♥♥♥♥'s mind, but it was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious to see him say that. [spoiler] (He said "in the end I was happy.")* [/spoiler]

What else do you expect from a visual novel? 

At least, surprisingly, the story was really fun to read, even though it having a cliche theme at its core. The storytelling was in a way addictive, and the whole ordeal was just fun. It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cheap on so many levels, that's why it's so fun to play it. Also the whole story was dependent on a so-called traumatic event. The build-up was solely about that and that only. I genuinely think the "plot twist" was a reach though. 

To be honest with you, it's easy to brush over this one but they actually put some thought over the story. Hello Everyone, 

I have inevitably gotten a “Bad End” in developer Arai Koh Create Office’s game “Bad End”. The Cursed Shadow is upon me and these are my final moments before I am snuffed out. Hopefully, these final words will help you survive longer than I did. 

In the words of Yuuji, “It is to late to stop now!”.

Bad End is a Horror themed Visual Novel that follows the life of Kyuuhei as he struggles to find the truth behind his best friends mysterious passing. The game starts off with Kyuuhei living out his life as a normal high school student, at least, that was until his best friend Yuuji decided that you wanted to try his hand at a infamous visual novel, known as “Bad End”. In the game, it is rumoured that if the player dies in the game, then they will also die in real life. Kyuuhei was sceptical about believing this rumour until his friend Yuuji mysteriously dies the next day. Doctors believe that his death occurred as a result of an unexpected illness. However, Kyuuhei believes that his friend may have died as a result of receiving a Bad End in the game “Bad End”. To test this theory, Kyuuhei decides to play the game for himself in order to find any clues that may lead him to the reason behind his friend’s untimely demise. 

The game operates in a traditional visual novel fashion, with the player having to read through a series of dialog and then being prompted to make various decisions that can have an impact on the game’s story. In this game players can experience a total of 14 different paths and as the game implies the majority of these endings are meant for players to receive a “Bad Ending”. However, there is also a rumour that it is possible to get a “Good Ending” in this game but at this time no one has survived long enough to find out. The paths that this game offer do tend to go from bad to worse pretty quickly but it can be interesting seeing where the story is going to go. Players should be able to beat this game within five hours or less, depending on reading speed/proficiency of the player. 

The game functions by the use of a mouse and the controls have been responsive. It is worth noting that if you play this game on the smart phone app, the games controls will be touch screen. However, I did not find any other significant differences (other than the PC having Achievements and Smart Phone version does not) between the smartphone version of the game and the PC version. This game was first released as a smartphone app and was eventually ported to PC.

While the player progresses through the novel, they can view the novel’s text box, stage backgrounds and character images. The game does have options for Saving, Loading, Skipping, Auto Play, and Text History; however, these functions can only be accessed when pausing the game.  This is rather unfortunate considering the game’s game play would have been smoother if these functions were just attached to the story’s text box. On the game’s pause menu, players can also view Achievements, Manual and Options tabs. The game’s setting tab is rather simplistic with options to only Slow/Speed Up text speed, increase/shorten Auto wait time, Skip settings, Volume up/down, and settings to have either full or windowed screen. 

The text on the main menu’s text screen has a unique design but that does not translate to the game’s story text boxes. The background environments are rather forgettable and provide nothing stunning. The character sprits in the game have more detail than the background environment and look pretty decent in game scenes. The character sprits are not animated but do transition frequently enough that the characters do not feel lifeless.  The game’s sound track is nice to listen to as you go through the game and did not detract from gameplay. For the majority of my gameplay, I did not run into any issues other than the game’s text randomly skipping scenes in the game. This is something that the developers said they intend to fix in a future update but for the time being it is possible that this glitch could occur during gameplay. It happened to me three times during my playthrough. 

With all that said, I have to say that I really enjoyed playing my way through “Bad End”. The game does have some minor discrepancies, but it still does have a rather interesting narrative. Regardless of the game being classified as a “Horror Visual Novel”, I would not say that I found it all that frightening. I would recommend this game to gamers that enjoy playing visual novel style games, are looking for a odd story, or to users that just want to try and see if they would be interested in the visual novel genre. 

Now with that said, I think we can bring this review to a close. I hope you found this review helpful and hope you are having a nice day.

[b]BAD END[/b] is the first game on Steam by the Japanese studio [i]Arai Koh Create Office[/i] and published back in 2015, quickly becoming a Very Positive title.

In [b]BAD END[/b] we take a concept that has been previously explored in movies and TV Shows, but rarely seen in Visual Novels. Best friends Kyuuhei and Yuuji have known each other for over 10 years, but recently Yuuji is focused on playing [b]BAD END[/b], a video game that recently made waves across the Internet due to deadly rumours circulating around it. According to the online opinion, those who die in the game, also die in real life.

When Yuuji finally finds a way to download the game app on his phone, his life is suddenly taken away. Cause of death? Heart failure! Strange as is seems, Kyuuhei decides to dive into the world of [b]BAD END[/b] himself, to discover the truth. The mobile game takes him to a Visual Novel where two girls from highschool fight to survive from a strange demonic shadow.

Storywise the game dive players between horror and the psychological side of the classic Japanese grudges. It’s not gory per say, but rather thrilling and pushes the mystery alongside the narrative. The plot develops at a nice pace and it’s likewise well produced. [b]BAD END[/b] might be predictable midway through the end, but still delivers some nice unexpected events!

The gameplay of [b]BAD END[/b] is pretty much your traditional Visual Novel with multiple endings. The idea is to go through the mobile game without dying and each decision counts towards one step closer to the truth. Players can always save the game as decision paths come along, and since each ending unlocks an achievement, it’s relatively easy to track them.

It’s much more fun to play blindly and try to survive. The game tolerates one death, but the second shall be your end. For those who aim at their best, the game also registers your very first playthrough in order to assign players with a rating. The longer you survive, the higher will the rank be. It’s a nice addition for those aiming at the challenge.

Visually, the game presents a nice mix between anime-based renders and 3D generated backgrounds. The characters are well drawn, with nice details and quite the attention to their expressions. The backgrounds have a nice structure and the 3D option delivers the perfect opportunity to use special colors to emphasize the horror effects.

Special scenes are delivered with amazing dedicated drawings depicting the scene with really good art direction. Almost worth of an anime show. Unfortunately theses scenes are rare and short, otherwise the whole production value would greatly increase. Although none of the renders are interactive the overall presentation is quite dynamic and appealing.

When comes to optimization [b]BAD END[/b] offers Full Screen mode and Windowed. When in Windowed mode the default resolution is 720p, and on contrary to other games / engines, it’s not possible to costume the size the resolution. Full Screen mode might upscale but for those playing at 1080p and higher the quality will remain pretty decent.

The Soundtrack shows a tremendous potential, avoiding generic electronic music, or any orchestral type of genre that’s so common among other games. Instead, players can appreciate some mystic guitar chords with intense vibrating waves of ambient and special effects. Too bad they become repetitive, otherwise would be another high selling point.

[b]BAD END[/b] is a 5 hour long Visual Novel where choices have intense results. It’s not extremely violent, but still delivering thrilling moments. A good mystery horror for the Halloween, one that might even surprise you positively, especially if purchased during a special sale.

[h1]Kurz zur Geschichte[/h1]
Es macht ein Gerücht von einem Handyspiel die Runde, das diejenigen töten soll, die ein schlechtes Spielende erreichen.
Unser Protagonist, Kyuuhei, macht sich nichts aus diesen Gerüchten bis sein bester Freund, Yuuji, plötzlich verstirbt nachdem er erzählt hat, dass er "Bad End" spielt.
Aber hängt der Tod seines Freundes wirklich mit dem Spiel zusammen? 
Um die Wahrheit heraus zu finden bleibt nur eines, und zwar das Spiel selbst zu spielen.

[h1]Fazit[/h1]
Wer schon japanische Horrorfilme wie z.B.  着信アリ(Chakushin ari) One missed call oder 呪怨 ( Ju-On ) The Grudge gesehen hat, der weiß auch ungefähr was ihn hier erwartet. 
Es gibt zwar keine Geisterfrau mit langen schwarzen Haaren aber jede Menge andere bekannte Elemente aus diesem Genre. Trotz, oder gerade wegen, der Bedienung von Klischees ist [i]Bad End[/i] aber sehr unterhaltend. 
Ganze 13 "Bad Endings" und 1 "True Ending" erwarten einen in diesem Visual Novel und veranschaulichen was der Hass, die Eifersucht und das Misstrauen eines Menschen für Ausmaße annehmen kann.
